text:
ellie: Quick heads-up: we've got sporadic mtls failures in apac after yesterday's key alias swap. Seeing ~5% handshake errors from apac-edge pool.
tariq: I pulled proxy traces: client Hello -> server cert send -> client abort with `certificate_verify_failed`.
jin: kms-bot alerted: KMS AccessDenied for `Encrypt` on apac-ca-key around the same timeframe.
kms-bot: event: 2026-03-28T14:12:07Z principal=svc-certd@apac node=apac-node-12 action=Encrypt result=AccessDenied
sec-oncall: do we have CloudTrail entries? Need to know if this is key policy or IAM.
ellie: grep CloudTrail -> multiple AccessDenied entries from assumed-role `certd-role` to key arn:aws:kms:apac:123:key/ca-2024-rot. Error message: "Caller is not authorized to use this KMS key".
tariq: that message typically means key policy blocks the principal. Did the alias switch create a new key id with a different policy?
jin: confirmed: alias `apac/mtls-ca` pointed to new key id at 14:09Z; the new key's resource policy was templated but missed the apac regional role list. CI didn't catch it.
sec-oncall: mitigation options: 1) create a short-lived Grant for certd-role 2) patch key policy to include principal 3) revert alias to old key. Fastest safe is Grant.
ellie: created grant at 14:17Z: `create-grant --key-id <id> --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123:role/certd-role --operations Encrypt --name certd-temp`
kms-bot: grant created by ellie at 2026-03-28T14:17:09Z id=gr-0a1b2c
tariq: after grant, handshake errors dropped to ~0.6% within 45s. Good.
jin: root cause: key templating step failed to inject regional principals when key was created via terraform.
sec-oncall: follow ups for compliance and engineering: - export CloudTrail AccessDenied events (attach to ticket) - update terraform template to include per-region role ARNs automatically - add integration test that simulates `kms:Encrypt` via `SimulatePrincipalPolicy` or dry-run grant - prefer using Grants in rollout scripts to avoid policy churn
ellie: I'll open SEC-CHANGE-2026-11 with artifacts and mark as mitigated.
tariq: also add a preflight in keystore pipeline: after new key creation, run `aws kms get-key-policy` and assert expected principals present. Fail the pipeline if not.
jin: and add metric `kms_access_denied_count` for certd in monitoring so we detect this faster.
sec-oncall: filing incident ticket and pinging compliance for audit trail. Monitoring for 2h.
ellie: thanks, cc @compliance https://internal.corp/audit/6487654321
sec-oncall: closing thread; status: mitigated -> monitoring.
